findings.route_reason: Undercuts acceptance criterion 1 (the red-first case must pin recipe-slice equals served item text) and makes a committed artifact dishonest: the case triage note and the eval_adapter comment both claim the endpoint payload is pinned, which the mutation disproves.
findings.claim: The one behavior D12 actually adds — the endpoint serving the NORMALIZED bytes rather than the raw filing — is pinned only by a text-grep on a local variable name, so a one-character mutation makes /api/normalized/{token} serve the raw filing while ui-offset-reproduction-contract stays green.
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/web/app.py:291 binds `norm = hit[2]`; WIRE_NORMALIZED (src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py:1637-1652) pins the Response(...) and X-Normalized-SHA256 expressions but never pins where `norm` comes from. Changing app.py:291 to `norm = hit[1]` (the raw filing bytes) leaves both pinned expressions intact: the endpoint then serves raw HTML with a matching sha header, and step 3 of the published recipe fails for every consumer on every run. The same hole covers `_run`: truncating `norm = result.get('normalized_text') or ''` (app.py:145) to [:100] also stays green.
findings.repro: sed -i '' 's/    norm = hit\[2\]/    norm = hit[1]/' src/sec10k/web/app.py && python3 -m evals.run --suite invariant  ->  [PASS] ui-offset-reproduction-contract, 60/60 = 1.000
findings.acceptance: Either add `norm = hit[2]` (and `norm = result.get('normalized_text') or ''`) to the WIRE_NORMALIZED allow-list so the mutations above go red, or make the case walk the endpoint for real; watch the hit[1] mutation fail first, then pass after revert. If neither is taken, the case triage note and the eval_adapter comment must stop claiming the endpoint payload is pinned, and the TODO debt row must say the served-bytes half is unpinned, not just the FastAPI binding.

findings.route_reason: Routed to repair despite LOW severity by orchestrator judgment: the broken line is inside the README recipe section this PR exists to publish, it is the deliverable rather than an adjacent nit, and the fix is one line in a file already open for R1. findings.claim: The README worked snippet uses an equality assert that is false for any item longer than 40,000 characters, so a consumer who changes the item or the fixture gets an AssertionError from the documented recipe.
findings.evidence: README.md:134 — `assert text[item['start']:item['end']] == item['text']`. build_view sets `text = raw[:DISPLAY_MAX]` with DISPLAY_MAX = 40_000 (src/sec10k/web/view.py:22,92). It holds for the printed example only because aapl-2025 item 1 is 16,053 chars; item 1A of the same fixture is 68,162 chars and the identical line fails. The prose parenthetical at README.md:136 warns about this but the code above it does not do what the prose says.
findings.repro: python3 -c "from src.sec10k.extract import extract_items; from src.sec10k.web.view import build_view; v=build_view(extract_items('evals/fixtures/aapl-2025/filing.htm')); i=[x for x in v['items'] if x['item']=='1A'][0]; print(i['chars'], len(i['text']), i['truncated'])"  ->  68162 40000 True
findings.acceptance: The snippet compares prefixes (e.g. assert text[item['start']:item['end']][:len(item['text'])] == item['text']) so it is true for every item, or it explicitly slices to DISPLAY_MAX; the eval RECIPE lines need no change since they already state the correct rule.
